transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-10 11:00 AM PT — Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Samir (Arborlytics Head of Platform), Lea (NetOps), Jonas (InfoSec)
---
[00:00] Maya: ok, uh, thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes, quick agenda — egress acceptance, TLS/KMS handshake questions from security, kernel/quant upgrades, and then next steps, sound good?
[00:12] Samir: yep, sounds good. Lea has the latest telemetry, I think she wanted to show a couple of heatmaps.
[00:17] Lea: yeah, thanks. so we ran three runs over the weekend across us-west and eu-central, baseline versus redwood private routed through our VPC peering, most interesting thing is 95th and 99th percent — occasional spikes to 420ms for small prompt workloads, while baseline avg is 120ms, so we're trying to figure out where that's coming from.
[00:39] Carlos: okay, thanks lea. can you confirm if those spikes correlated with MTU or with the quantized kernel switchover?
[00:45] Lea: initial suspicion is MTU mismatch on the bridge to the appliance, we saw a couple of PMTU blackholes during one test. also there was a canary kernel roll on friday, but those spikes preceded the rollout.
[01:00] Maya: so two threads — networking path (MTU/peering) and runtime kernel/quantization. carlos, you mentioned you ran a quick trace?
[01:06] Carlos: yep, I pulled the tracing and saw repeated TCP retransmits between the peering edge and the private nodes, with MSS reductions. it's subtle — the NVMe health checks on the host also pushed some background load at the same time, so tail latency amplified. I'll attach the flame view.
[01:22] Jonas: from security side we were mostly worried about the TLS handshake failures we saw on 2026-03-07 — a small percentage of requests failed with 'handshake_timeout' and then retried, two things: are keys rotating mid-session? and do we have audit events for those errors?
[01:38] Priya: we do capture audit logs; maya i'll follow up on details. carlos can you explain difference between handshake failures and KMS errors we've seen?
[01:45] Carlos: sure. handshake_timeout often comes from either network jitter causing TCP delays, or from the KMS agent not returning the wrapped key in time. in our env that showed as a 503 from the KMS client library before failover. we have fallback cached unwrapped keys for a small time window but if the rotation is aggressive you'll see more timeouts.
[02:03] Samir: we have strict rotation, it's every 24 hours for the test key. is that too aggressive?
[02:08] Carlos: 24 hours is fine normally but with our current KMS latencies on your side (you have a chained HSM proxy) combined with the network MTU issues, the compounded latency pushes some of those operations over the threshold. we suggest a short-term mitigation: extend rotation window for the pilot to 72h and enable local KMS caching TTL to 10 minutes while we stabilize.
[02:27] Samir: ok i'll take that back to ops, that seems reasonable for the pilot.
[02:31] Lea: quick note — we already toggled off jumbo frames on the bridge and that cut down a class of PMTU problems, but the peering link still has some fragmentation at 1500->9000 boundaries. we need a deeper MTU bake.
[02:45] Carlos: thanks — also, we recommended enabling continuous prefix KV cache for the most frequent prompt prefixes; that reduces token generation lambda and reduces tail. i'll send the sample config.
[02:56] Maya: great. on kernel upgrades, carlos you had a plan for v1.8 that included rollback gates?
[03:02] Carlos: yes. plan: staged canary 10% for 6 hours, then 50% 24h, monitor 99th pct and error rate. if 99th increases >20% or error rate >0.5% we rollback. also we have a preflight test to run quantized model regression on a 1k prompt set. note: v1.8 changes allocator behavior which affected small-batch latencies in our internal cluster once; we want to validate memory compaction flags.
[03:25] Samir: would you run the regression against our real prompt set or just synthetic?
[03:29] Carlos: ideally both — we can run a fast pass on synthetic and a slower pass on your top-200 prompts. that will give us signal for correctness and tail.
[03:38] Lea: how long would the top-200 take? we want to schedule maintenance windows carefully.
[03:42] Carlos: with our harness and a 4-GPU test rig you'll get results in ~3 hours. I can parallelize to cut it down.
[03:50] Jonas: on logging — when there is a handshake timeout we need a correlated trace id in our SIEM. are you able to push trace ids in the audit log records?
[03:58] Priya: yes, we already emit 'request_trace_id' and 'kms_request_id' in the audit bundle, but we'll add the explicit mapping to the runbook we share.
[04:06] Maya: ok so immediate actions: 1) carlos runs ingress/egress microbench including MTU emulation and will attach CSVs; 2) priya shares security pack and runbook; 3) maya sends updated pilot pricing. anything else?
[04:17] Samir: can we also get a quick schematic of fallback routing? we saw a misroute to a lower-tier region during high load last thursday.
[04:24] Carlos: yes, that was due to an incorrect priority in the routing policy — the fallback tier had lower cost-topology and the smart-router favored it. we patched the policy but we'll run a replay to be sure and propose a stricter cost delta threshold.
[04:36] Lea: replay would be great, please include the iptables/nft rules snapshot for the node so we can compare.
[04:42] Carlos: will do.
[04:44] [04:45] Samir: quick question — commercial, if we go dedicated after pilot what kind of reserved capacity commitments do you expect?
[04:52] Maya: for a team at your scale we'd propose a reserved pool mapping: X GPU months for base throughput with a 6-12 month commit — i'll send a sketch with numbers but we can be flexible for the POC to convert.
[05:03] Samir: ok thanks.
[05:06] Jonas: security question — do you support customer-managed HSM or only Redwood-managed?
[05:11] Priya: we support both. for private deployments you can bring your own HSM and we integrate via standard KMIP or cloud KMS plugins. for the hosted control plane we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in most clouds. we'll share specific integration docs.
[05:24] Jonas: great, and audit retention windows? we need 2 years for compliance.
[05:29] Priya: we can export logs to your S3 and also retain on Redwood for 90 days by default; extended retention add-on available — i'll include options in the pack.
[05:39] Lea: back on the MTU matter — we have a scheduled maintenance window friday 2-4pm PT, could we run a joint canary and do the kernel reg there?
[05:48] Carlos: yes that's workable. prefer do the kernel preflight earlier to catch regressions, but network changes in that window are ideal. we recommend: preflight Thursday night, kernel canary in maintenance window, and rollback window through saturday morning.
[06:02] Maya: scheduling note — can we do a dry-run handoff checklist so the netops team knows who pushes what?
[06:08] Carlos: I'll draft the step-by-step: preflight commands, collector flags to enable, how to flip routing priority, and how to trigger fallback.
[06:15] Samir: perfect. last item — we saw a small number of incoherent tokens after quantized model update last month, is that expected?
[06:23] Carlos: with certain quantization profiles you can see rare grounding drift on edge cases; our optimize team recommended a mixed-precision profile for your workload which preserves fidelity with a small cost uplift. we can run a quality regression alongside perf.
[06:36] Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[06:40] Priya: i'll upload the SOC2 pack and the KMS checklist by Wednesday, march 11.
[06:46] Carlos: i'll run the ingress/egress microbench and the top-200 prompt regression, attach CSV and trace snippets by March 15.
[06:53] Maya: i'll send pilot commercial sketch and reserved capacity options by March 12 and schedule the canary rehearsal for week of March 22.
[06:58] Samir: i'll confirm IP allowlist targets and the downstream service list by March 17.
[07:02] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll capture these in the follow-up note — priya can you circulate the recording and the action item list?
[07:09] Priya: yes will do, recording + notes in slack #pilot-arborlytics and google drive link: https://drive.redwood/demo/pilot-arborlytics-attachments (note: placeholder link)
[07:17] Samir: one last quick ask — can you include a short doc on the fallback cost delta thresholds you apply? our finance team wants to understand cost impact of fallback to higher-cost model variants.
[07:26] Maya: yes that's in the pricing sketch i'll share.
[07:29] Carlos: i'll also include a small script that simulates fallback routing and shows token cost delta in the CSV.
[07:34] Maya: perfect. thanks all, meeting adjourned.
---
Post-call notes: references mentioned in call: pilot telemetry heatmap (Lea), kernel v1.8 release notes (internal link), SOC2 package (Priya), pilot pricing sketch (Maya), ingress/egress microbench script (Carlos).
